newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 16.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 16.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday:

* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones industrial average ended up 52.73 points at 7,975.71, surpassing its July 8 record finish of 7,962.31, as investors largely shook off the effects of some high-profile earnings warnings early in the second quarter.
* Cement giant PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa said on Tuesday it proposed a spinoff and sale of its 50.1 percent shareholding in PT Indofood Sukses Makmur.
* Indonesian financial markets calmed on Tuesday after being jolted by recent currency volatility in the region, analysts said.

* On Tuesday, the Jakarta composite index ended down 0.29 points, or 0.04 percent, at 722.21 points as the market focused on Indocement after the cement giant said it planned to sell its 50.1 percent stake in noodle maker Indofood, brokers said.
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,455.00/6.00 at 0250 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,455.00/2,7.00.
* Indocement and Indofood after Indocement said it planned to sell its 50.1 percent stake in noodle maker Indofood.
* Maharani Intifinance as the multifinance firm is scheduled to be listed on Wednesday.

* Conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers following a report which quoted drug maker and distributor Inovax Ltd in Sydney as saying a consortium led by the Bakrie Group was expected to have majority control of the company once an acquisition was completed later this calendar year.

* Banking stocks following the government decision to limit loans for land purchase and development. Also after Moody's Investors Service said it was revising its ratings outlook for Indonesia's state banks to uncertain from stable pending a decision on planned mergers among the seven institutions.
* Fishery firm Daya Guna Samudera after a news report that the government had revoked import duty on fish caught in Indonesia's exclusive economic zone.

* Indonesian petrochemical company PT GT Petrochem Industries ADMG.JKL, a member of the Gajah Tunggal Group, said on Monday a wholly-owned subsidiary GTPI Netherlands B.V. had signed a $300 million syndicated term loan facility with 22 financial institutions. The firm said the loan would be used to strengthen its financial performance and expand production.

* Small-capitalised metals firm PT Alumindo Light Metal Industries on a report that the International Finance Corporation, a World Bank unit, said it would provide loans worth $35 million to fund the firm's expansion plans.
